lesson.title: Sequences and the memory that fades
lesson.subtitle: One symbol at a time

video.title: Sequences and the memory that fades: One symbol at a time
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours. Narration in the lesson language. Captions are separate files.
cast: Joseph - computer studies teacher, talking to a fellow lecturer
Narrator - the Darsi voice, warm and precise, talking to a university lecturer

scenes.narration: Students say the net reads the sentence. Point them at the end number with the slider on the left: the sentence is gone.
In the seminar: one symbol at a time, and a number that fades before you name vanishing gradients.
A sequence is read one symbol at a time. The hidden state is the only memory the next symbol will see.
Each step keeps only a share of that state. If the share is near zero, the cue is gone after a few empty steps.
Near one, the sign of the cue is still there at the end. That is the limit of this simple net: a long gap washes the start away.
Here is how much of the cue is left. A weak memory keeps almost none, and a strong memory keeps most of it.
Quick check! Three empty steps follow a cue, and the memory is near zero. What is left at the end?
Almost none of the cue. A small memory, multiplied again and again, washes the start away.
Students write the end number at two slider positions before you name the idea. Then they move the slider and correct the prediction.
Your turn. Does a recurrent net read the whole sequence in one look?
Remember this. The hidden state is the memory, and a long gap fades it. Attention, next, looks back instead.
Try it in your next lecture. Predict the end number, then slide, then correct the prediction.

checkpoints.prompt: Three empty steps follow a cue, and the memory is near zero. What is left at the end?

options.text: A new cue the net invented

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: a small memory, multiplied at every empty step, washes the cue away.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: near zero, almost none of the cue is left.

checkpoints.prompt: Does a recurrent net read the whole sequence in one look?

options.text: No, one symbol at a time

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: it reads one symbol at a time and hopes the hidden state kept the rest.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: it never sees the whole sequence at once.
